periods.analysis: We open 2024-Q3 at 13% complete and green, which is the right starting posture for work that has to be disciplined, not flashy. The signing bonuses for hard-to-staff subjects are complete, and HR has already tied the first awards to math, special education, bilingual science, and CTE aviation-pathway vacancies near the airport corridor. The early-career mentorship program launch is in-progress, with principal-nominated mentor teachers being matched by grade band and subject cluster. The exit-survey + retention dashboard is not-started, due in the later build sequence, so for now we are relying on vacancy reports, resignation codes, and school-by-school staffing huddles.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green start by protecting the hard-to-staff bonus pool through the October hiring window and publishing a weekly vacancy heat map for principals. Move the mentorship launch from design to operating rhythm by confirming mentor rosters, stipends, and first-meeting dates for every teacher hired since July 1. Begin the dashboard groundwork now by standardizing exit-survey questions before the data team starts the formal build.

periods.analysis: Progress moved from 13% to 19% complete, a +6 percentage point quarter-over-quarter gain, and the initiative remains green. That is steady, responsible movement: the completed signing bonuses are helping Harborview compete in a tight regional labor market, especially for secondary math and special education positions. The mentorship program is still in-progress, and the Teaching and Learning team piloted Wednesday release-period check-ins at East Harbor High, Mariner Middle, and Bayview K-8. The exit-survey + retention dashboard remains not-started, which is acceptable at this stage but cannot drift because we need sharper reasons for midyear departures.
periods.recommendations: Extend the bonus strategy by adding a principal verification step so incentives are tied to actual classroom vacancies, not generic staffing projections. Keep the mentorship program moving by requiring each pilot site to submit attendance, mentor-mentee match quality, and first-60-day concerns by the end of the quarter. Prepare the dashboard work by assigning a data owner in HRIS and reserving time with the city-schools analytics vendor before spring budget season.

periods.analysis: In 2025-Q1, completion increased from 19% to 25%, another +6 percentage point quarter-over-quarter movement, with green status maintained. The throughline is encouraging: bonuses are complete and no longer a concept on paper, while principals report they are most useful when paired with faster screening for credentialed applicants. Mentorship remains in-progress, and the first cohort of 42 early-career teachers is now grouped into elementary literacy, secondary STEM, special education, and newcomer-language learner circles. The exit-survey + retention dashboard is still not-started, and that is the one watch item inside an otherwise healthy quarter because anecdote is not a retention strategy.
periods.recommendations: Sustain momentum by keeping the applicant screening standard at five business days for bonus-eligible positions. Extend mentorship to include one classroom observation cycle per early-career teacher, using trained mentor release time rather than asking new teachers to carry the coordination burden. Start the dashboard requirements document now, including fields for school, subject, years of service, stated reason for leaving, and whether housing affordability or commute distance is cited.

periods.analysis: The initiative advanced from 25% to 31% complete, a +6 percentage point quarter-over-quarter gain, and remains green. This is the kind of measured execution I like to see: not a burst of activity followed by drift, but a predictable build across hiring, support, and data. The completed signing bonuses are now feeding the spring recruitment calendar, including offers for high-need roles before candidates commit to neighboring districts. Mentorship is still in-progress, with mentor teachers using Harborview’s HARBOR observation protocol to focus on classroom routines, family contact, and chronic-absenteeism response practices. The exit-survey + retention dashboard remains not-started, so the next risk is that we celebrate hiring wins without fully understanding preventable exits.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the green trajectory by locking early contracts for hard-to-staff hires before the summer transfer cycle opens. Expand mentorship from the pilot schools to all campuses with three or more first- or second-year teachers, and give principals a simple monthly completion report. Convert the dashboard from concept to project charter by approving the data dictionary and integration plan with HR, payroll, and school assignment tables.

periods.analysis: Completion moved from 31% to 37%, again a +6 percentage point quarter-over-quarter increase, and the status stays green. The initiative is now past the launch-and-learn phase and into the harder work of consistency across a fast-growing district. Signing bonuses remain complete and are being used with more precision, including targeted outreach to dual-certified special education/math candidates and bilingual educators for port-area and westside schools. The mentorship program remains in-progress, with summer institute sessions converted into monthly learning labs so new teachers do not lose support after orientation. The exit-survey + retention dashboard is still not-started, which I will continue to call out plainly because retention decisions should be made from evidence, not hallway memory.
periods.recommendations: Sustain bonus effectiveness by comparing acceptance rates for bonus-eligible offers against non-bonus offers after the first 30 days of school. Extend the mentorship model by adding a rapid-response support visit for any early-career teacher whose classroom has substitute coverage for more than three days in a month. Move the dashboard forward by completing security review and confirming which resignation and transfer codes will be visible to principals.

periods.analysis: In 2025-Q4, the initiative rose from 37% to 43% complete, a +6 percentage point quarter-over-quarter movement, with green status maintained. We are seeing the benefit of staying boring in the best sense: completed bonuses, repeatable mentorship routines, and fewer last-minute scrambles in the highest-need subjects. Mentorship is still in-progress, and the district has added peer observations on Routes 7 and 14 school clusters so teachers can see strong practice without losing a full day to travel. The exit-survey + retention dashboard remains not-started, and as winter resignations begin to appear, that gap becomes more visible even though the overall initiative is healthy.
periods.recommendations: Keep the green performance by renewing bonus eligibility criteria before the next recruitment fair, with explicit priority for special education, math, science, bilingual education, and CTE. Deepen mentorship by training assistant principals to use the same coaching look-fors, so feedback to new teachers is aligned rather than contradictory. Set a firm dashboard kickoff date and require a prototype view for superintendent cabinet review before the spring hiring season.

periods.analysis: Progress increased from 43% to 49%, another +6 percentage point quarter-over-quarter gain, and the initiative remains green. At nearly the halfway mark, the work is showing maturity: the completed signing bonuses are now part of a broader recruitment package rather than a standalone inducement. Mentorship remains in-progress, with 68 early-career teachers receiving structured support through mentor logs, classroom visits, and content-specific planning sessions. The exit-survey + retention dashboard is still not-started, and I am watchful here because Harborview’s growth, housing costs, and regional commute pressures can quietly erode retention if we do not measure them. Green does not mean passive; it means the system is strong enough to act before the numbers turn.
periods.recommendations: Sustain recruitment strength by pairing each bonus offer with a 48-hour onboarding call covering certification, relocation questions, and school placement. Extend mentorship by prioritizing teachers in schools with elevated chronic absenteeism, where classroom stability is especially important for student connection. Open the dashboard work immediately with a minimum viable product focused on voluntary exits, hard-to-staff roles, and first-three-year teacher retention.

periods.analysis: The initiative moved from 49% to 55% complete, a +6 percentage point quarter-over-quarter increase, and closes this sequence in green. That steady climb from 13% in 2024-Q3 to 55% in 2026-Q2 tells me the team has built a durable operating cadence rather than chasing one-time announcements. The signing bonuses for hard-to-staff subjects remain complete and are now embedded in recruitment planning for the next school year. Mentorship remains in-progress, with mentor coverage mapped by campus and subject, and principals are using the end-of-year conferences to identify which early-career teachers need summer support. The exit-survey + retention dashboard is still not-started, and it is now the clearest unfinished management tool in an otherwise well-managed initiative.
periods.recommendations: Protect the green status by carrying forward the bonus pool and publishing a summer hiring calendar with decision deadlines for every hard-to-staff vacancy. Extend mentorship into a year-two retention bridge, including June planning sessions and August classroom setup support for returning early-career teachers. Prioritize the exit-survey + retention dashboard as the next deliverable, with a 90-day build plan, named HRIS owner, and first report focused on preventable departures by school, subject, and years of service.

periods.analysis: 95% complete. 2 of 3 milestones are done. Next up: Exit-survey + retention dashboard (due Oct 24, 2026).
periods.recommendations: No action needed. Continue on the current plan.
